sn12.24:1.5: Sāriputta, like his teacher, seeks out meaningful discussion with people who are not Buddhist.
sn12.24:3.1: In [sn12.17]() and [sn12.18]() we have already encountered non-Buddhist ascetics, both of whom asked about kamma in a similar way. The popularity of such discussions shows kamma was a hot topic of the day, with many different ideas about what it was, how it worked, or if indeed it was real.
sn12.24:3.6: The wanderers frame their question carefully and respectfully, hence Sāriptta answers them directly and affirms their manner of questioning.
sn12.24:4.3: The wanderers have already shown their epistemological caution, so, in identifying “contact” as the key dependency, Sāriputta indicates one of the most directly observable factors of dependent origination. But contact is also a key underlying cause of wrong views ([dn1:3.45.1]()).
sn12.24:6.1: Sāriputta clarifies the meaning of “dependent”: it is something without which the other cannot be experienced, i.e. it is a necessary condition.
sn12.24:8.5: The explicit affirmation and repetition of information reinforces the correct text in the memory and wards off creeping disinformation.
sn12.24:17.2: Compare with _attho vutto_ in the Itivuttaka. Here the sense is that the topic can be summed up with one statement.
sn12.24:21.9: The Buddha recapitulates, confirming that the sequence here goes back only as far as the six senses. This agrees with [dn1:3.71.12](), which likewise goes back to the six senses. There, the factors beginning with ignorance are implied under wrong view.
